nodes.label: constants.ts
nodes.summary: Central constant definitions for the Pāvati Pustak trust management platform. Defines all role enumerations (PRIMARY_ADMIN through COLLECTOR), role ordering for hierarchy, payment modes (CASH, UPI, MIXED), donation categories and statuses, privacy levels, member statuses, join modes, receipt statuses, notification statuses and channels, audit action types, page size constants with millimeter dimensions, and suggested donation amounts. Also exports derived TypeScript union types for each constant group.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `as const` assertions throughout to produce literal union types. Employs a Record-based pattern for label maps (e.g. ROLE_LABELS, PAYMENT_MODE_LABELS). Extracts union types from const objects using indexed access types like `(typeof ROLE)[keyof typeof ROLE]`. All exports are named.
nodes.languageLesson: The `as const` + indexed access type pattern is a lightweight alternative to TypeScript enums, preserving both runtime string values and compile-time type narrowing without enum overhead.

nodes.label: permissions.ts
nodes.summary: Role-based access control (RBAC) permission system for the trust platform. Defines 36 granular permission strings organized by resource (trust, member, donation, receipt, template, campaign, announcement, report, settings, notification, audit, donate). Maps each TrustRole to an explicit array of granted permissions, where PRIMARY_ADMIN receives ALL_PERMISSIONS and lower roles receive progressively fewer. Includes a fallback `permissionsForRole()` function, a complete PERMISSION_LABELS map for UI display, and an `everyone` baseline permission set that every authenticated user inherits.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports `ROLE` and `TrustRole` from constants.ts. Uses spread syntax with `...everyone` and `...ops` to compose permission arrays declaratively. The ALL_PERMISSIONS array is derived from PERMISSION values. Permission strings follow a `resource:action` naming convention.
nodes.languageLesson: Composing permission arrays with spread of shared base sets (everyone, ops) is a common RBAC pattern that avoids duplication while keeping each role's full grant list explicit and auditable.

nodes.label: schemas.ts
nodes.summary: Comprehensive Zod validation schemas for all trust platform input forms and API endpoints. Covers authentication (login, register, forgot/reset password, Google OAuth), trust CRUD (create, update), member management (add, update), donation creation with payment splits and cross-field validation, campaign and announcement management, receipt template configuration with nested field configs, notification settings, profile updates, password changes, and reusable validators for phone (Indian 10-digit), email (strict regex with disposable-email blocking), slugs, and amounts. Exports inferred TypeScript types for each schema. Also exports a curated list of 30 disposable email domains blocked during registration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Zod library (`z` namespace). Defines reusable validators (`phone`, `email`, `vals()`) at the top. The `vals()` helper converts const objects to Zod enum tuples. Uses `.superRefine()` on createDonationSchema for cross-field split-amount validation. Exports inferred types via `z.infer<typeof schema>`. Re-exports `phone`, `phoneOrEmpty`, and `SUGGESTED_AMOUNTS` from constants for consumer convenience.
nodes.languageLesson: Zod schemas serve as the single source of truth for both runtime validation and compile-time types via z.infer, eliminating the need for separate interface definitions of input shapes.

nodes.label: types.ts
nodes.summary: TypeScript interface definitions for all domain entities in the trust platform. Defines 14 core interfaces: User (authentication profile), Trust (organization with settings and privacy flags), TrustMember (membership link with role and permissions), Donor, Donation (with status, payment mode, privacy, and optional splits), Receipt, ReceiptFieldConfig (template positioning metadata), ReceiptTemplate, PaymentCampaign, Announcement, NotificationLog, AuditLogEntry, and composite types TrustMemberWithUser, TrustWithStats, and AuthSession. Each interface mirrors the Prisma database schema structure with string-typed IDs and ISO date strings for API transport.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports types from both constants.ts (TrustRole, DonationCategory, etc.) and permissions.ts (Permission). Uses optional properties extensively for nullable database fields. Composite interfaces use intersection-like patterns (TrustMemberWithUser extends TrustMember with required user). Uses union literals for authProvider and ReceiptFieldConfig alignment.
nodes.languageLesson: Separating domain interfaces from validation schemas (types.ts vs schemas.ts) allows the type system to describe data shapes while Zod handles input validation — a clean separation of concerns where schemas validate inbound data and types describe runtime state.

edges.detail: Imports ROLE constant object and TrustRole type for permission-to-role mapping
Imports JOIN_MODE, PAYMENT_MODE, PRIVACY, ROLE, and SUGGESTED_AMOUNTS for schema enum definitions and default values
Imports ALL_PERMISSIONS array and Permission type for member permission update schema validation

Imports 11 domain types (AuditAction, DonationCategory, DonationPrivacy, DonationStatus, JoinMode, MemberStatus, NotificationChannel, NotificationStatus, PageSize, PaymentMode, ReceiptStatus, TrustRole) for interface field typing
Imports Permission type for TrustMember.permissions field and PermissionInput export
Exports inferred TypeScript types (CreateTrustInput, CreateDonationInput, etc.) that serve as API input types, complementing the domain interfaces in types.ts
ROLE_PERMISSIONS record uses ROLE constant keys and TrustRole type; all permission arrays reference the role hierarchy defined in constants
Schemas reference constant values for enum definitions (vals(ROLE), vals(PAYMENT_MODE), etc.), default values (SUGGESTED_AMOUNTS), and validation constraints
All entity interfaces use types derived from constants (TrustRole, DonationStatus, PaymentMode, etc.) to type their fields
